primeros-7-dias.title: First 7 days clean
primeros-7-dias.subtitle: A basis to start without condemnation.
primeros-7-dias.description: Seven days to organize the heart, activate a spiritual routine and make small decisions that sustain freedom.

days.title: Today starts with grace
days.verse: Base Reading: Lamentations 3:22-24 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
The first day of freedom is not built on pride, but on mercy. Maybe you arrive with fatigue, guilt or fear of failing again. But God does not begin speaking from condemnation; He begins by reminding you that his love was not exhausted last night, nor this morning, nor in your worst moment. Grace does not erase responsibility, but it does change the place from which you respond. You no longer fight for God to love you; You fight because you are loved.

Today you don't need to promise a perfect life. You need to take a faithful step. Addiction is fueled by secrets, impulses and isolation; Freedom is fueled by light, concrete decisions and dependence on Christ. This day may seem small, but before God it counts. A clean day is a seed. An honest decision is a door. A sincere prayer is a return. Don't walk around looking only at what you left behind; Look at the God who walks with you and renews his mercy every morning.
days.question: What small, visible and concrete decision will make this first day different?
days.prayer: Father, I receive your mercy to begin without condemnation. I don't want to hide or promise from my strength. Guide me today with simple and faithful steps.
days.practice: Define your most vulnerable time of day and prepare an escape action: go for a walk, call someone or leave your cell phone far away.

days.title: Take care of your tickets
days.verse: Base Reading: Proverbs 4:23-27 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Keeping your heart does not mean living in fear; It means recognizing that your interior is worth too much to leave without direction. What enters your eyes, your conversations, your searches and your habits forms desires. Sometimes we think that the problem begins when we fall, but many falls began long before: in an account that we follow, a schedule without limits, an ambiguous conversation, a curiosity that we did not stop in time.

God does not call you to a narrow life to take away your joy. It calls you to a protected life so that you can love freely. Taking care of your tickets is a form of worship. That is to say: my heart belongs to Christ, and not everyone has the right to disciple me. Today look at your cell phone honestly. It is not about hating technology, but about putting it under the lordship of Jesus. If something pushes you towards the occult, you don't need to negotiate; you need to obey early. Freedom grows when you learn to close doors before you are on the edge.
days.question: What digital, emotional or relational input do you need to limit today?
days.prayer: Jesus, teach me to take care of my heart without fear and without a double life. Give me wisdom to recognize small doors before they become chains.
days.practice: Delete, silence or block an account, search or app that usually opens a dangerous door.

days.title: Don't negotiate in secret
days.verse: Base reading: 1 Corinthians 10:12-13 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Temptation almost never comes screaming. It comes as a private conversation: 'just look', 'just a minute', 'no one's going to find out', 'you've had enough'. If you agree to talk for too long, you end up defending what you initially knew you should cut. That is why the Bible does not invite us to flirt with temptation, but to seek the way out that God provides.

The way out is almost always easier than we want to admit: get up, turn off the screen, write to someone, change places, pray out loud, open the Word, drink water, leave the room. Quick obedience seems exaggerated only when we still want to negotiate. Don't measure your maturity today by how close you can get to the edge without falling; measure it by how quickly you run to Christ when you recognize danger. God does not leave you alone in the face of impulse. He provides a way out, but you must take it. Grace does not replace decision; strengthens it.
days.question: What will be your first action when temptation appears?
days.prayer: Lord, give me speed to take the exit that you provide. I don't want to talk to that which destroys me.
days.practice: Write your emergency plan in a short sentence and post it where you can see it.

days.title: Renew the mind
days.verse: Base Reading: Romans 12:1-2 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
It is not enough to empty your life of bad content; the heart needs to be filled with truth. Many try to win only by resisting, but resistance without renewal is exhausted. God wants to transform the way you think, desire, rest and respond. Purity is not just saying 'no'; It is also learning to love what is good, clean, true and eternal.

Renewing the mind takes time. Every reading, every honest prayer, every healthy limit and every conversation in light retrains your interior. Maybe today you still feel old impulses, but that doesn't mean nothing is changing. A renewed mind begins when you decide not to automatically feed the old pattern. Instead of asking 'how far can I see without falling?', ask 'what brings me closer to Christ?' Deep freedom is not born from an empty mind, but from a mind inhabited by the truth of God. Today let the Word not only inform you, but form you.
days.question: What old thought do you need to replace with a truth from God?
days.prayer: Holy Spirit, renew my mind. It changes my desires, my internal arguments, and my way of responding when I am vulnerable.
days.practice: Memorize a short Bible truth and repeat it three times during the day.

days.title: Walk accompanied
days.verse: Base reading: Ecclesiastes 4:9-12 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Shame will tell you that you have to figure this out just so you can present yourself clean to others. But Christian freedom almost never flourishes in isolation. God uses people to sustain us, correct us, listen to us, and remind us of the truth when our minds become clouded. You don't need to tell everyone everything, but you do need to stop living as if no one can accompany you.

Walking accompanied does not mean depending on the approval of others. It means accepting that you were created for community. An honest message can break the power of a secret. A shared prayer can sustain a difficult night. An uncomfortable question asked by someone who loves you can help you wake up. The enemy prefers that you fight in silence because silence magnifies the lie. Today take a step towards the light. Look for someone mature, trustworthy, Christ-centered, who does not treat you with morbidity or condemnation. Freedom needs truth, but it also needs company.
days.question: Who could accompany you with wisdom, prayer and truth?
days.prayer: Father, give me humility so as not to walk alone. Guide me to healthy people who help me stay in the light.
days.practice: Send a short message asking for prayer or accountability this week.

days.title: Celebrate the small
days.verse: Base Reading: Zechariah 4:10 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
A clean day matters. A night when you turned off your cell phone matters. A search you didn't do matters. A conversation you decided not to open matters. Freedom is often built with small obediences that no one sees, but God does. Don't despise the day of small beginnings just because you don't see a complete transformation yet.

Addiction accustoms you to thinking in terms of all or nothing: if I wasn't perfect, I failed; If I had a bad thought, I already lost; If I'm tired, it doesn't count. The gospel teaches you another rhythm: walk, confess, receive grace, obey, walk again. Celebrating the small is not settling for little; It is recognizing the work of God in the process. Gratitude strengthens perseverance. Today look at your progress without pride and without contempt. Thank God for a concrete victory. What seems small today can become an altar of memory for tomorrow.
days.question: What small victory can you recognize without becoming inflated and without despising it?
days.prayer: Father, thank you for every real step. Teach me to celebrate what you are forming without falling into pride or condemnation.
days.practice: Write down a small victory today and turn it into a prayer of gratitude.

days.title: remains
days.verse: Base Reading: John 15:4-8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Completing seven days is not the end goal; It's a sign that you can start to form a rhythm. Jesus did not say: 'spread your strength and produce fruit.' He said: remain in me. Freedom is not sustained by willpower alone, although will matters. It is sustained by a living relationship with Christ, where you return again and again to his presence, his Word, his community and his grace.

Staying means not treating God as only an emergency button. It means learning to walk with Him on good days, tense days, boring days, and vulnerable days. If this week was clean, don't trust yourself as if you were already invincible. If it was difficult, don't conclude that nothing helped. The fruit ripens permanently. Today look forward with humility: what pace are you going to maintain? What limit will still be active? Which person will continue to accompany you? Jesus didn't just help you get started; He wants to teach you to live united with Him.
days.question: What spiritual and practical rhythm are you going to maintain next week?
days.prayer: Jesus, I want to stay in you more than trust in my strength. Bear fruit in me with patience, truth and love.
days.practice: Choose the following devotional plan or schedule your reading for tomorrow.

cuando-recai.title: when I relapsed
cuando-recai.subtitle: Restoration without hiding.
cuando-recai.description: A plan to return to God after a fall, without denying sin and without surrendering to shame.

days.title: Don't hide
days.verse: Base Reading: Genesis 3:8-9 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
After falling, the first reaction is usually to hide: close the app, act normal, silently promise that it won't happen again, avoid praying because you feel like you have no right. From the garden, shame tries to convince us that God comes mainly to crush us. But God calls: 'Where are you?' Not because it ignores your location, but because it wants to invite you out of the darkness.

Returning to God after a relapse does not begin with perfect spiritual performance. Start with an honest answer: here I am, this happened, I don't want to hide anymore. Honesty does not minimize sin; It puts him in the only place where he can be treated with grace and truth. If you fell, don't turn the fall into an identity. Don't cover it with excuses either. Come to the light. God does not heal what we insist on making up. Today your first step is not to punish yourself; It is to present yourself before the Father with truth, because Christ opened the way to return.
days.question: What part of this fall have you wanted to hide or justify?
days.prayer: Father, here I am. I don't want to run away from you or make up for what happened. Receive me in your truth and lead me to repentance.
days.practice: Pray out loud an honest sentence about what happened, without excuses and without insulting yourself.

days.title: Confess to heal
days.verse: Base reading: 1 John 1:8-9 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Confessing is not informing God something He did not know. To confess is to stop fighting against the truth. Relapse gains power when it becomes shrouded in secrecy, guilt, and self-deception. Confession opens a window. Allow grace to enter with its own name: not 'I failed in general', but 'this is what I did, this is what I sought, this was the lie I believed'.

God's faithfulness is firmer than your instability. His forgiveness is not permission to repeat sin; It is cleansing to get up without carrying a condemnation that Christ has already carried. But true confession also looks at patterns. What happened before? Loneliness, anger, tiredness, boredom, easy access, a conversation, a social network? Don't just confess the fruit; look at the root. God does not want you to live in cycles of fall and empty promise. He wants to form a transparent life in you, where the truth stops being a threat and becomes medicine.
days.question: What do you need to confess with a specific name, not with general phrases?
days.prayer: Jesus, I confess my sin and receive your forgiveness. Cleanse me, but also show me the pattern I must change.
days.practice: Write down three things that happened before the relapse: emotion, place, and access.

days.title: Break the lie
days.verse: Base reading: John 8:31-36 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Before a relapse there is almost always a lie at work. Sometimes he says, 'I need it to calm me down.' Other times: 'I've had enough'. Sometimes it is disguised as resignation: 'this is who I am', 'I will never change', 'God is already tired of me'. Lying not only pushes towards sin; also try to define yourself after falling.

Jesus does not offer freedom through empty motivational phrases. He says the truth sets us free. That truth includes who God is, who you are in Christ, and what sin actually produces. Today identify the specific lie that led you or left you trapped. Then respond with a biblical truth. It is not enough to say 'this is wrong'; you need to say what is true. If the lie was 'I am alone', respond: God is close to the broken. If it was 'I cannot resist', answer: God provides a way out. If it was 'I already lost', answer: in Christ I can rise and walk in light.
days.question: What lie did you believe before, during or after the fall?
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, expose the lie and establish me in your truth. I don't want to live directed by thoughts that enslave me.
days.practice: Write a lie and a biblical truth that contradicts it.

days.title: repair the road
days.verse: Base Reading: Hebrews 12:12-13 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Repentance is not just about feeling bad; is to change direction. If a route led you to fall, don't leave it the same hoping that the next time will be different. Grace does not eliminate the need for practical wisdom. If the problem was an app, change access. If it was a schedule, change the routine. If it was loneliness, look for company before you reach the limit. If it was tiredness, order your rest.

Mending the road can feel humbling, even uncomfortable. Maybe it means recognizing that you are not as strong as you thought. That is not failure; It is wisdom. God does not ask you to show strength by leaving doors open. It invites you to make straight paths for your feet. Each concrete adjustment is a spiritual statement: I am not going to facilitate what Christ is removing from my life. Don't make an abstract promise today. Make a visible repair. Freedom becomes more real when obedience takes shape in concrete decisions.
days.question: What specific route do you need to correct to avoid repeating the same cycle?
days.prayer: God, give me humility to change what I must change. I do not want to protect access to that which enslaves me.
days.practice: Make an adjustment today: screen limit, lock, remove access, or change your schedule.

days.title: Return to the community
days.verse: Base reading: James 5:16 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Shame will tell you that you can only return to the community when you are better. The gospel says that healing often begins when you stop pretending. Confessing to a mature person does not replace confession to God, but it can help you break the isolation where the fall is repeated. You don't need to look for someone curious, harsh or reckless; You need someone who loves Christ, keeps confidentiality and points you to the truth.

Healthy community is not about humiliating exposure. It's about accompaniment. Someone who can ask how you are, pray with you, celebrate progress, and help you see patterns when you're tired. Relapse tries to convince you that you are the only one. You are not. There are others fighting, healing and learning to live in light. Today take a cautious step towards someone. Don't wait to feel worthy of support. Receiving help is also a form of repentance, because you recognize that you were not created to win in secret.
days.question: Who can you approach with humility and without spiritual theater?
days.prayer: Lord, guide me toward healthy community. Free me from hiding and looking for people who do not help me walk in truth.
days.practice: Send a simple message: 'I need prayer and accompaniment this week.'

days.title: Receive discipline with love
days.verse: Base Reading: Hebrews 12:10-11 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
After a fall, setting boundaries can feel like punishment. But in Christ, discipline is not rejection; It is training. A loving Father is not satisfied with seeing you trapped in a cycle that destroys you. Corrects you for life. That can mean discomfort: less access, more transparency, clearer schedules, difficult conversations, new routines. Discomfort does not mean that God is far away; It may be evidence that he is training you.

Don't confuse grace with absence of structure. Grace receives you, and then teaches you to walk differently. If everything remains the same after the relapse, you are probably not taking seriously what God wants to heal. Today he receives discipline as care. Do not impose measures on yourself out of self-hatred, but out of love for the life that Christ is forming. The question is not: 'what punishes me the most?' The question is: 'what helps me to remain free with humility?'
days.question: What loving boundary do you need to accept for a while?
days.prayer: Father, teach me to receive correction without condemnation. May my limits be born from love and not self-hatred.
days.practice: Set a limit for seven days and share it with someone you trust.

days.title: Raise your head
days.verse: Base reading: Micah 7:7-8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
A relapse can be serious, but it has no final authority over your story. The risen Christ does not call you to deny what happened; calls you to arise with truth. Raising your head is not pride. It is faith that God's grace is stronger than condemnation, and that the Spirit can form a new obedience in you.

Look at what you learned this week: what led you to fall, what lie you believed, what access you need to repair, what help you need. That information is not to punish you; It is to walk with more wisdom. The enemy wants you to use the fall as proof that there is no future. God can even use this experience as a point of return, humility and dependence. Don't turn relapse into home. Make this day an altar of return. Freedom is not measured by never needing grace, but by learning to quickly return to Christ and walk in the light.
days.question: What did you learn from this fall that you don't want to forget?
days.prayer: Jesus, lift me up with humility. I don't want to deny my sin, but I also don't want to live defined by it.
days.practice: Choose the next plan and write a concrete decision for the next seven days.

ansiedad-y-soledad.title: Anxiety and loneliness
ansiedad-y-soledad.subtitle: When the void seeks screen.
ansiedad-y-soledad.description: Seven readings to recognize anxiety, loneliness and emotional need without running to content that does not heal.

days.title: Name what you feel
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 139:23-24 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Many times the impulse does not begin as sexual desire, but as a nameless emotion. Anxiety, boredom, sadness, rejection, tiredness or loneliness look for a quick way out. If you don't know how to name what happens inside, the screen becomes an easy anesthetic. But what is not named usually governs in secret.

God is not afraid of your emotions. The psalmist asks God to examine the heart because he knows it needs help to see itself clearly. Today don't immediately run to correct yourself; first stop to discern. What's underneath the impulse? In need of comfort? Rage? Feeling of failure? Desire to feel control? Naming it before God does not make it more dangerous; puts it in light. Anxiety loses some of its strength when it stops being a confusing cloud and becomes a concrete sentence. Christ wants to meet you not only in your behavior, but in the emotion that precedes it.
days.question: What specific emotion lies beneath the impulse to escape to the screen?
days.prayer: Lord, examine my heart with tenderness and truth. Help me name what I feel without running away or hiding.
days.practice: Pause for two minutes, breathe slowly and write down a specific emotion before picking up your cell phone.

days.title: God is near
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 34:17-18 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Loneliness has a strong voice. He says no one understands, no one watches, no one cares if you fall. That voice can become especially intense when you're home alone, late at night, or after a day of rejection. But Scripture reveals a God close to the broken, not distant from the weak.

The closeness of God is not always felt as an immediate emotion. Sometimes it is received by faith: choosing to speak to him even if you don't feel anything, opening the Word even if you are dry, asking for help even if you are embarrassed. Your need for company is not a sin; It was created to find an answer in God and in a healthy community. The problem appears when we try to fill a legitimate need with something that leaves us even more empty. Today take your loneliness to Christ before taking it on a search. He does not despise your need. He can accompany you to the exact place where you normally seek anesthesia.
days.question: At what time of day does your feeling of loneliness become stronger?
days.prayer: Father, come to me in this vulnerable place. Teach me to seek your presence rather than false relief.
days.practice: Before opening networks or a browser, pray a simple phrase: 'God, I feel alone; come with me'.

days.title: Not all relief heals
days.verse: Base reading: Jeremiah 2:12-13 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
There are reliefs that promise water and leave you thirsty. Sexual content may feel like relief, control, or comfort for a few minutes, but it often leaves shame, distance, and more emptiness. Jeremiah speaks of abandoning the fountain of living water to dig broken cisterns. That image describes very well the escapes that cannot sustain the soul.

Ask yourself honestly: what brings about this relief after finishing? More peace or more anxiety? More love or more isolation? More freedom or more need to hide? Wisdom does not evaluate only immediate pleasure; look at the fruit. Christ does not compete with cheap anesthetics by offering a momentary thrill. He offers life that can sustain you even when the emptiness doesn't immediately go away. Today make a different choice. When you feel inner thirst, don't run to the broken cistern first. Name your need and look for a real source: prayer, Word, a call, rest, movement, silence before God.
days.question: What quick relief leaves you feeling emptier afterward?
days.prayer: Jesus, I want to drink from you and not from broken fountains. Teach me to distinguish momentary relief from true healing.
days.practice: Trade an impulse for a restorative action: water, walking, breathing, praying, or calling someone.

days.title: The body also speaks
days.verse: Base reading: 1 Kings 19:4-8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Sometimes we treat every temptation as if it were solely a problem of will, but the body also participates. Tiredness, hunger, stress and lack of sleep lower emotional resistance. In the story of Elijah, God does not begin with a lecture; He gives him rest and food. There are times when a wise spiritual decision begins with taking care of the body God gave you.

This does not mean justifying sin because you are tired. It means recognizing real vulnerabilities. If you know that after midnight you lose clarity, do not turn that hour into an open field. If when you are exhausted you are looking for quick dopamine, organize your rest. If stress pushes you to escape, learn to release it in healthy ways. The body is not the enemy of the spiritual life; It is part of your stewardship. Today listen to the basic signals: did you sleep? did you eat? did you move? did you rest? God can also strengthen you through simple habits.
days.question: What physical need are you ignoring and then spiritualizing?
days.prayer: Lord, help me take care of my body as part of my obedience. Give me humility to rest before I break.
days.practice: Do a physical action before night: real food, water, a walk, or going to bed earlier.

days.title: Search for human voice
days.verse: Base reading: Romans 12:15-16 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
A screen can distract you, but it cannot accompany you like a person. Many falls occur because the soul needs to be heard and ends up accepting stimulation as a substitute for connection. God made us to cry with those who cry and rejoice with those who rejoice. Community is not accessory; It is part of heart health.

Seeking human voice doesn't always mean an hour-long deep conversation. It can be an honest audio, a short call, a message: 'I am vulnerable today, can you pray for me?' Pride will say that is too much. Shame will say that you are annoying. But wisdom knows that asking for help early avoids greater pain. Don't wait until you're on the edge. Loneliness is fought before it becomes an impulse. Today identify a safe person. Not to be your savior, but to remember that Christ also cares for you through the body of Christ.
days.question: Who can you contact before isolating yourself?
days.prayer: God, take me out of isolation. Give me people of peace and humility to let me accompany you.
days.practice: Send a concrete message: 'Today I need prayer, I am vulnerable.'

days.title: Pray with your own name
days.verse: Base Reading: Philippians 4:6-9 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Anxiety often feels like noise. Many worries together, without a clear shape. Paul invites us to present requests to God. Not just general religious thoughts, but concrete requests. Prayer is not denying anxiety; It is bringing it into the right presence. When you pray with your own name, you stop carrying a confusing mass and begin to deliver real parts of your life.

Today don't just say: 'Lord, help me.' That's good, but go deeper. Say: 'I'm anxious about this conversation', 'I feel rejected', 'I'm afraid of being alone', 'I want to escape because I feel insufficient'. The peace of God does not always come as an explanation; many times it comes as a guard over the heart. Prayer puts a sentinel where there was once panic. After praying, think about what is true, noble and pure. Don't leave your mind empty. Fill it with what Christ approves.
days.question: What specific request do you need to present to God today?
days.prayer: Lord, I give you my anxiety with its own name. Guard my heart and direct my thoughts toward your truth.
days.practice: Write down three specific concerns and turn them into three short sentences.

days.title: Build healthy shelters
days.verse: Base Reading: Psalm 46:1-3 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Don't wait for the critical moment to build shelter. When anxiety and loneliness are already screaming, deciding well becomes more difficult. That is why wisdom prepares paths before needing them. A healthy refuge can be a nightly routine, a person to write to, a prayer list, a walk, a worship playlist, digital boundaries, or an activity that brings you back to the body and the presence of God.

God is our true refuge, but he also teaches us to create structures that remind us of his refuge. Maturity does not consist of living improvising each battle, but rather preparing spaces where grace is more accessible than escape. Today design your refuge map. What will you do when you feel anxious? What will you do when you feel alone? What will you do when it's late and you're tired? Don't leave it to the emotion of the moment. Preparing yourself is not a lack of faith; It is wise obedience.
days.question: What healthy shelter can you prepare before the next vulnerable night?
days.prayer: Father, you are my refuge. Teach me to build visible rhythms that help me run towards you.
days.practice: Create a list of three actions for anxiety and three actions for loneliness.

identidad-en-cristo.title: Identity in Christ
identidad-en-cristo.subtitle: You are not your worst moment.
identidad-en-cristo.description: A plan to remember who you are in Christ when shame tries to give you a name.

days.title: Son before fighter
days.verse: Base Reading: John 1:12-13 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Your struggle is real, but it is not your name. Pornography and compulsive masturbation can try to define you as a slave, hypocrite, weak or impossible. Shame loves to turn a pattern into an identity. But the gospel begins elsewhere: in Christ you receive the right to be a child of God. Before being someone who fights, you are someone who is received.

This changes the way we fight. If you fight to earn the love of the Father, each setback becomes a sentence. If you fight from the love of the Father, each step of obedience becomes a son's response. God does not reduce you to your worst night. Nor does he ignore what must be healed. He calls you son to rise with dignity, truth and responsibility. Today don't use insults as if they were humility. Saying 'I'm trash' is not holiness; It is forgetting what Christ bought. True humility is recognizing sin without denying the identity that God gives.
days.question: What false name have you accepted about yourself?
days.prayer: Father, help me fight as a beloved son, not as an orphan trying to deserve your gaze.
days.practice: Repeat throughout the day: 'In Christ I am a son before my struggle.'

days.title: Purchased with price
days.verse: Base reading: 1 Corinthians 6:18-20 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Digital culture treats the body as a product: something to consume, display, compare, or use. The gospel says something radically different: your body matters to God. It is not trash, it is not an enemy and it is not an escape tool. It was bought with a price. Christian purity is not born from contempt for the body, but from honoring it as part of a life dedicated to Christ.

When you fall, you may feel disgusted with yourself. But God does not call you to hate your body; It calls you to surrender it. Honoring God with your body includes your eyes, your hands, your sleeping habits, your digital decisions, your sexuality, and your way of treating others. The question changes: not 'what can I do without anyone finding out?', but 'does this honor the God who bought me with love?'. Today look at your body with reverence, not with idolatry or contempt. Christ paid too much for you to live divided.
days.question: What concrete decision honors your body as belonging to Christ?
days.prayer: Jesus, thank you for buying me with love. Teach me to live in my body with honor, self-control and gratitude.
days.practice: Do an action of bodily honor: rest, eat well, move, or set a digital limit.

days.title: New creature
days.verse: Base reading: 2 Corinthians 5:16-17 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
There are stories that explain wounds, but they have no right to govern your future. Maybe you grew up exposed to sexual content, experienced abuse, rejection, abandonment, or learned to use the screen as a refuge. God does not minimize that. But in Christ, your story doesn't end where it began. The new creation does not mean that everything disappears immediately; It means that a new life began to operate within you.

Sometimes you'll look at old patterns and think, 'nothing changed.' But deep transformation usually grows like a seed. You start to notice what you previously normalized. You start to hurt for what you previously justified. You begin to ask for help, set limits and return to God faster. Those are signs of new life. Don't define yourself by the slowness of the process. Define your hope by the work of Christ. Today speak to your past from your present identity: that happened, that hurt, that influenced, but it is not my lord. Christ is doing something new.
days.question: What part of your past do you continue to use as a sentence about your future?
days.prayer: Lord, make your new creation visible in me. Heal my history and teach me to walk as someone renewed.
days.practice: Write a sentence: 'My past explains part of my history, but Christ defines my future.'

days.title: Temple of the Spirit
days.verse: Base reading: 1 Corinthians 6:19 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
God does not live far from your daily life. His Spirit does not stay outside your room, your cell phone, your nights and your impulses. If you are in Christ, your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. That should not produce panic, but rather reverence and hope. You're not trying to win from an empty room; God himself dwells in you to form new desires.

This truth confronts the double life. There is no spiritual space and no other secret where God does not have a voice. But it also consoles: in the moment of vulnerability you are not abandoned to your impulse. You can stop and say: Holy Spirit, guide my eyes, my body, my mind. Purity is not just human self-control; It is the fruit of the Spirit working in a surrendered person. Today practice presence. Before making a digital decision, remember: God is here. Not as a policeman waiting to destroy you, but as a holy presence that wants to give you life.
days.question: How would your day change if you remembered that the Spirit dwells in you?
days.prayer: Holy Spirit, fill my thoughts, my desires and my decisions. Teach me to live conscious of your presence.
days.practice: Before opening a vulnerable app, pause and pray: 'Holy Spirit, guide me.'

days.title: Without condemnation
days.verse: Base Reading: Romans 8:1-4 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Conviction and condemnation may look alike at first, but they produce opposite fruits. Conviction says: come to the light, this must change, Christ has grace for you. Condemnation says: hide, there is no hope, you are disgusting. One brings you closer to God; the other pushes you into the secret. In Christ there is no condemnation, because the condemnation was carried by Jesus.

This does not soften the sin. It makes it treatable. If you believe that God only wants to crush you, you will hide until the next fall. If you receive that Christ removed the condemnation, you can repent with seriousness and hope. Many do not move forward because they confuse hating themselves with repenting. True repentance looks to God, not to the destroyed self. Today, when you hear guilt, ask yourself: does this lead me to Christ or does it close me in on myself? The voice of the gospel does not deny evil; announces that you are no longer condemned to live under his rule.
days.question: Are you responding to conviction or condemnation?
days.prayer: Jesus, thank you that in you there is no condemnation. Lead me to deep repentance, free from self-destruction.
days.practice: Write two columns: 'condemnation says' and 'gospel answers'.

days.title: Call for freedom
days.verse: Base reading: Galatians 5:1, 13-16 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Christ does not free you to live without direction; It frees you to love. Christian freedom is not doing everything that impulse asks, but rather ceasing to be governed by desires that destroy. Before you thought that saying yes to impulse was freedom. Then you discovered that it left you less free. The Spirit calls you to a deeper freedom: to be able to choose the good, to love without using, to look without consuming, to rest without escaping.

Standing firm in freedom implies vigilance. Old chains sometimes call with a familiar voice. Not because they are good, but because they were customary. Today remember that freedom cost the blood of Christ. Don't treat it like something cheap. But don't carry it like an impossible weight either. Walk by the Spirit. That means depending on God in small decisions: what I watch, what time I sleep, who I talk to, what I do when I'm alone. Freedom is practiced in everyday life.
days.question: What old slavery is trying to sound like freedom?
days.prayer: Christ, affirm me in the freedom you purchased. Teach me to use my freedom to love and not to return to chains.
days.practice: Identify an everyday decision where you will practice freedom today.

days.title: Loved and sent
days.verse: Base reading: Ephesians 5:1-2 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Your identity in Christ does not end with surviving temptation. God wants to form in you a life that reflects his love. You are a beloved child, and beloved children learn to imitate the Father. That means that your freedom process is not just for you. One day, your healed story may become encouragement to someone who still feels trapped.

You don't need to rush to teach before you heal. But you can begin to see your struggle with a redemptive gaze. God does not waste surrendered tears. Every boundary, every confession, every day of obedience, and every humble return is building compassion. Healthy identity produces healthy mission. You are not a damaged project hiding in a corner. You are someone loved, formed and sent to live in light. Today finish this plan by looking at Jesus and also looking at others with compassion. The freedom you receive can become a refuge for someone else.
days.question: How might God use your process to better love others?
days.prayer: Father, thank you that I am loved in Christ. Form in me a life that reflects your love and helps others walk in light.
days.practice: Pray for a person who also needs freedom, even if you don't know their full story.

pureza-digital.title: Digital purity
pureza-digital.subtitle: Order for your screens.
pureza-digital.description: A practical plan to form a holier, freer and more conscious relationship with your cell phone.

days.title: Your screen disciples
days.verse: Base Reading: Psalm 101:2-3 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Your screen is not neutral. Every app, algorithm, account and recommendation trains something in you: attention, desire, comparison, impatience, curiosity or gratitude. Not all explicit content starts out explicit. Sometimes it starts as entertainment that lets your guard down, sexualized humor, bodies normalized as consumption, or a video chain that slowly pushes you toward what you vowed to avoid.

The mature question is not just: 'is this a sin?' It's also: 'what is he turning me into?' David talks about walking with integrity even inside the home. Today your home includes your private screen. Digital purity does not seek to demonize technology, but to place it under the lordship of Christ. You can use digital tools to learn, work, pray and connect. But if you do not choose intentionally, others will disciple your desires for you. Today look at your screen like a garden: what are you watering? What weed grows without permission? Freedom begins when you stop consuming automatically.
days.question: What app or type of content is discipling your desires more than you admit?
days.prayer: Lord, govern my digital life too. Teach me to use technology for life and not for slavery.
days.practice: Check your home screen and move a debilitating app out of sight.

days.title: Limits like love
days.verse: Base reading: Proverbs 25:28 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
A boundary is not a prison when it protects something valuable. Proverbs compares a person without self-control to a city without walls. The walls did not exist to take away the freedom of the inhabitants, but to protect life, families, crops and the future. In the same way, digital boundaries protect your heart from inputs that you won't always be able to handle in real time.

Culture will tell you that freedom is unlimited access. But if anything has the power to drag you into shame, unlimited access is not freedom; It is exposure. A limit can be a schedule, a filter, a shared password, sleeping away from your cell phone, not using incognito, eliminating a network for a while, or deciding not to be alone with a screen at certain times. Don't set limits only after you fall. Put them as an act of love towards the person that God is forming in you. Today don't ask what the minimum acceptable limit is. Ask which limit best helps your freedom.
days.question: What specific limit would be love towards your future?
days.prayer: Father, give me self-control and humility to accept limits. May my walls protect life, not appearance.
days.practice: Set a digital boundary for seven days and write it down as a visible commitment.

days.title: Cut the dark curiosity
days.verse: Base Reading: Ephesians 5:8-14 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Dark curiosity disguises itself as innocent: an ambiguous word, a profile, a link, a comment, a search that you can still justify. Many falls do not begin with an open decision to sin, but with a small exploration that negotiates with the light. Paul does not say to play with the works of darkness to demonstrate strength; He says that we live as children of light.

Being a child of light means cutting early. You don't need to investigate how much danger there is. If the content awakens a part of you that wants to hide, you already have enough information. Quick obedience protects clarity. Dark curiosity promises control, but it often ends up controlling you. Today practice a simple rule: when something starts to move you towards secrecy, I close. I don't explain, I don't prove, I don't follow. Christ does not call you to live paranoid, but awake. Light does not need to negotiate with darkness to be compassionate; it simply remains light.
days.question: What kind of curiosity usually opens a dangerous door for you?
days.prayer: Jesus, make me a child of light also in my searches, recommendations and digital conversations.
days.practice: Defines a cutting phrase: 'This does not suit me; I'm closing now.'

days.title: Regain attention
days.verse: Base reading: Colossians 3:1-4 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Digital purity is not just about avoiding pornography. It's also about reclaiming your attention for God, your family, your calling, your body, and your present. A mind fragmented by constant stimuli is more vulnerable to rapid impulses. When everything distracts you, any strong desire seems urgent.

Setting our sights on things above does not mean ignoring the earth. It means ordering life from Christ. Your attention is a form of worship because what you look at repeatedly ends up seeming bigger. If all day long you feed comparison, sensuality, anxiety and noise, don't be surprised if at night your soul is restless. Today it recovers a space without a screen. At first you may feel uncomfortable because the silence reveals what the noise covered up. Stay. Pray. Walk. Read. Talk to someone. Let your mind remember that it was not created to live dragged by notifications.
days.question: What area of your life deserves more attention than it is receiving?
days.prayer: Father, reorganize my attention. May my mind learn to look towards Christ and not just towards quick stimuli.
days.practice: Do 20 minutes without a screen and use that time for prayer, walking, or reading.

days.title: Bring out the hidden
days.verse: Base reading: Luke 8:16-17 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Technology facilitates double lives: deleted history, alternate accounts, hidden tabs, secret schedules. But the occult is not only a moral problem; It is also an emotional burden. Living in hiding fragments the soul. Jesus calls us to the light not to humiliate us, but to heal us. What remains hidden usually grows in power; what comes to light can be treated with grace.

Transparency does not mean that everyone has the right to know everything. It means you don't build a private realm where no one can ask. It may include accountability agreements, filters, honest conversations, or stopping using certain digital spaces alone. The light may feel threatening at first, but over time it becomes restful. Not having to hide so much is part of freedom. Today identify a digital place where you've been keeping too much of a secret. Invite Christ there and take visible action.
days.question: What part of your digital life needs the most light?
days.prayer: Lord, I don't want to live divided. Give me courage to bring to light what needs to be healed.
days.practice: Share a digital decision you are making with someone you trust.

days.title: Use technology for life
days.verse: Base Reading: Philippians 4:8-9 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
The Christian solution is not to hate all technology. It is learning to govern it under the truth. The same cell phone that was a door to fall can become a reminder of prayer, Bible reading, community, music that edifies, notes of gratitude and calls for support. The question is who is directing whom.

Paul invites us to think about what is true, noble, just, pure, lovely and worthy of praise. That also applies to your screens. It is not enough to remove destructive content; Fill space with life-forming content. Organize your digital environment so that the good is closer and the destructive is further away. This does not guarantee absence of temptation, but it changes the friction. Making the holy more accessible and the harmful less accessible is practical wisdom. Today he redeems a tool. Put a visible verse, reading app, prayer reminder, or support contact within reach.
days.question: How can your cell phone bring you closer to God instead of farther away?
days.prayer: Jesus, teach me to use my tools for life, truth and community.
days.practice: Put Clean4Jesus, Bible or a prayer note in a visible place on your screen.

days.title: Do maintenance
days.verse: Base Reading: Proverbs 4:25-27 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Digital purity is not set once and forgotten forever. Algorithms change, routines change, vulnerabilities change. What is ordered today can be disordered in silence. That's why you need maintenance: review access, schedules, apps, followed accounts, drop patterns and moments of fatigue.

Maintenance is not obsession. It's care. Just as you clean a house because you live in it, you review your digital life because your heart travels there every day. A weekly review can prevent a monthly relapse. Question: What is feeding me? What is draining me? What am I hiding? What limit worked? What should I adjust? Do it with God, not just with human strength. The goal is not to have a perfect screen, but rather an increasingly integrated life before Christ. Today design your maintenance rhythm so as not to depend solely on crises.
days.question: What weekly digital review are you going to keep?
days.prayer: Father, give me perseverance to guard my digital path with peace, clarity and truth.
days.practice: Schedule five minutes a week to review apps, accesses, schedules and risk signs.

volver-a-empezar.title: start over
volver-a-empezar.subtitle: Grace to get back on track.
volver-a-empezar.description: For seasons where you lost rhythm and need to return without drama, but firmly.

days.title: Start small
days.verse: Base reading: Matthew 11:28-30 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Starting over feels heavier when you try to do it with a huge promise: now I will never again, now I will be perfect, now I will change my entire life in one day. Jesus does not first invite the tired to present an impressive plan. He invites them to come. The return begins with approaching Him as you are, tired and needy.

Starting small is not conformity. It is humility. Freedom is built with real steps, not with intense speeches that last a night. Maybe today the step is to create the PIN, activate the refuge, read this devotional, write to someone or sleep without the cell phone. Small does not mean insignificant. A seed is small and yet it contains a future. Do not despise the obedient step because it does not solve everything. Christ forms people with rhythms, not just emotional moments. Today come to Him and take a step that you can truly obey.
days.question: What is the small, faithful step you can take today?
days.prayer: Jesus, I come to you tired. I don't want to promise from pressure; I want to walk from your grace.
days.practice: Choose a single obedient action for today and complete it before bed.

days.title: Don't dramatize, obey
days.verse: Base reading: John 14:15-17 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
When we lose rhythm, sometimes we do a lot of internal drama: we analyze, we blame ourselves, we imagine scenarios, we write big plans. But God many times has already shown us the next step. Simple obedience cuts through the noise. If you love Christ, keep his commandments. Not as an exchange to gain love, but as a response to someone who already loved you.

Today you don't need to understand your entire history to obey what you know. If you know that an app hurts you, limit it. If you know that the night is dangerous, prepare. If you know you need to talk, write. If you know that the Word sustains you, read. Simple obedience may feel unspectacular, but it has power. The Holy Spirit helps in the concrete, not only in the emotional. Don't wait until you feel great inspiration to do the right thing. Maturity is formed when you obey even without ceremony. Less drama, more small fidelity.
days.question: What simple obedience have you been putting off?
days.prayer: Lord, give me practical love. Help me to obey without turning each step into a theatrical battle.
days.practice: Make a pending obedience today before opening social networks.

days.title: Order your day
days.verse: Base reading: Ephesians 5:15-17 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Disorder opens doors. A day without structure can end up governed by fatigue, impulses and screens. Redeeming time doesn't mean filling every minute with anxious productivity. It means living awake, recognizing that your schedules also disciple your heart. If you know that certain empty spaces lead you to fall, do not leave them without direction.

Ordering your day is a form of spiritual care. Define when you will work, when you will rest, when you will read, when you will turn off the screen, when you will talk to someone. Temptation loses strength when it does not find so much improvised ground. This doesn't mean that everything will turn out perfect. It means you are not handing over the day to chance. God gives you wisdom to walk with intention. Today look at the next few hours, not your entire life. Where do you need structure? What moment will be vulnerable? What will you do before you get there? Freedom is often decided on the agenda rather than on impulse.
days.question: What part of your day needs structure so as not to be exposed?
days.prayer: Father, teach me to redeem time with wisdom and peace, not with anxiety.
days.practice: Plan your next three hours, including a screen-free break.

days.title: Accept help
days.verse: Base Reading: Galatians 6:1-2 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Starting over alone may seem more comfortable because no one asks and no one sees. But it is also more fragile. Paul calls to bear each other's burdens, not to pretend that they do not exist. There are burdens that become lighter when someone knows them, prays and walks with you.

Accepting help does not make you less spiritual. It makes you honest. Self-sufficiency is often disguised as maturity, but it is often fear of being known. Seek wise help: someone who will restore with meekness, not someone who will crush you; someone who loves the truth, not someone who minimizes sin; someone who points to Christ, not to control you. Today don't wait until you are 'better' to ask for support. Precisely by wanting to improve, it opens a door to the community. Freedom is not a solitary project. God uses human hands to sustain holy processes.
days.question: What burden do you need to stop carrying alone?
days.prayer: God, give me humility to receive help and discernment to seek healthy people.
days.practice: Ask for a quick chat with someone you trust this week.

days.title: Practice truth
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 51:6-12 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
God loves the truth intimately because healing begins there. Many relapses are sustained by small lies: 'I'm fine', 'it wasn't that bad', 'I can handle it', 'no one needs to know', 'I'll change tomorrow'. To practice truth is to let God enter the exact place where you normally justify yourself.

Truth is not just admitting guilt; It is also admitting need. I need to sleep. I need support. I need limits. I need to confess. I need to change this routine. The lie promises you comfort, but it costs you freedom. The truth may be uncomfortable at first, but it opens the way. David did not ask God for a better image; He asked for a clean heart and a firm spirit. Today practice truth with God and with you. Do not use religious phrases to avoid the concrete. Tell the whole truth, and then receive the whole grace. Christ does not heal characters; heal real people.
days.question: What uncomfortable truth do you need to accept before God?
days.prayer: Lord, you love the truth deeply. Form in me a clean heart and a firm spirit.
days.practice: Write down a common lie and replace it with a specific truth.

days.title: Recognize real progress
days.verse: Base Reading: Philippians 1:6 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Sometimes you despise progress because it is not yet perfection. But God does not despise the work he is beginning. If you read again, if you asked for help, if you set a limit, if you confessed, if you held out for one night, that's real progress. Not to inflate yourself, but to recognize that God is working.

Gratitude protects from discouragement. When you only look at what's missing, you can feel like nothing changes and end up giving up. But when you recognize God's faithfulness in concrete steps, your hope is strengthened. Paul trusted not in perfect human perseverance, but in the God who finishes what he begins. Today look at your process with honest eyes. Yes, there is no way. Yes, there are areas to heal. But there is also evidence of grace. Name them. Thank you. Then keep walking. Celebrating real progress is not lowering the bar; It is honoring the God who transforms step by step.
days.question: What evidence of progress can you recognize this week?
days.prayer: Father, thank you that you do not abandon the work you started. Help me recognize your grace without settling.
days.practice: Write down three signs of progress, even if they seem small.

days.title: Keep up the pace
days.verse: Base Reading: Hebrews 10:35-39 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Starting again is important, but staying requires rhythm. You can't live on emotional resets alone. You need a life that sustains what God is forming: Word, prayer, community, boundaries, rest and purpose. Perseverance doesn't always feel intense; It is often seen as a calm decision repeated for many days.

Hebrews remembers that we need perseverance. Not because God is stingy, but because the promise is inherited by walking. If this week helped you, don't close the plan as if you no longer need structure. Decide what's next. Another plan? A fixed reading time? A surrender partner? A night limit? Freedom matures when it stops depending only on crises. Today he establishes a small but sustainable rhythm. Don't aim to impress; aims to remain. Christ didn't just find you in the reboot. He wants to walk with you in continuity.
days.question: What pace are you going to maintain after this plan?
days.prayer: Jesus, give me perseverance. I don't want to live on reboots alone; I want to stay with you every day.
days.practice: Schedule your next reading and choose a plan to continue.

fortaleza-noche.title: Strength for the night
fortaleza-noche.subtitle: When he lets his guard down.
fortaleza-noche.description: Readings for the hours when fatigue, silence and cell phones become dangerous.

days.title: Prepare before
days.verse: Base reading: Matthew 26:40-41 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
The night is not conquered only at night. It is prepared before. Jesus told his disciples to watch and pray because the spirit may be willing, but the body is weak. That phrase is not an excuse; It is a compassionate diagnosis. God knows your limits. The question is whether you are taking them seriously.

If you know that at a certain time you lose clarity, prepare the ground beforehand. Decide where the cell phone will sleep. Define what you will do if the impulse appears. Have a prayer ready. Let someone know if you are vulnerable. Stop improvising at the weakest moment of the day. Preparing yourself does not mean that you do not trust God; It means that you obey with wisdom. Temptation loves to find you tired, alone and without a plan. Today go ahead. Don't wait until you have the screen in your hand to decide. Night victory begins with evening decisions.
days.question: What specific preparation do you need to do before night comes?
days.prayer: Lord, help me to watch and pray with humility. I don't want to rely on my strength when I know I'm vulnerable.
days.practice: Leave your cell phone charging out of bed or out of reach tonight.

days.title: Tiredness speaks
days.verse: Base Reading: Psalm 4:8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Tiredness may sound like temptation. Sometimes you don't need encouragement; you need to sleep. You don't need a search; you need to turn off. You don't need to feel control; you need to rest in God. When the body is exhausted, the mind seeks quick relief and lowers its defenses. The night magnifies emotions that look different in the morning.

The psalm talks about lying down in peace because God sustains. Sleep can also be an act of faith: recognizing that the world does not depend on you, that you don't have to solve your anxiety with a screen, and that your body needs care. Do not spiritualize exhaustion as if it were always a lack of holiness. Ask honestly: am I tempted or am I exhausted? It can be both, but the wise answer will include rest. Today honor God by turning off before. Tomorrow's peace can begin with the simple obedience of closing the night.
days.question: Are you interpreting tiredness as desire?
days.prayer: Father, give me peace to sleep and humility to recognize my exhaustion before seeking escape.
days.practice: Turn off screens 20 minutes before bed and prepare a calm routine.

days.title: Don't open a conversation
days.verse: Base Reading: James 1:13-15 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Temptation wants to talk. It doesn't always come as an order; It comes as a suggestion. 'Just check', 'just look', 'just remember', 'just try'. James describes a process: desire attracts, seduces, conceives and produces death. Wisdom is to cut off the process early, not to wait until the last second to demonstrate resistance.

At night, don't open a debate with what you already know hurts you. The tired mind is a bad lawyer. You can build arguments to justify what in the morning you would recognize as a danger. That's why you need simple rules: if it's late, I don't search; If I am alone, I do not sail without purpose; If I feel impulse, I get up; If I am vulnerable, I ask for help. You don't need to explain anything to temptation. You need to get out. God will not call you a coward for running away from what destroys your soul. Fleeing toward Christ is spiritual courage.
days.question: What internal conversation should you cut off before it grows?
days.prayer: Jesus, give me firmness so as not to negotiate at night. Help me get out early and run to you.
days.practice: When the urge comes, physically get up, drink water, and change places.

days.title: Delivery on the day
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 55:22 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Many overnight crashes begin with undelivered loads. Frustration, guilt, pressure, rejection, sadness or anger accumulate during the day and look for an outlet when everything falls silent. If you do not give those burdens to God, they may seek discharge in places that do not heal.

Before going to sleep, practice real surrender. Not a quick prayer to fulfill, but an honest conversation: this hurt me, this tired me, this scared me, this made me feel alone. God invites you to cast your burden on Him because He sustains. You don't have to carry your anguish to your pillow as if it were part of you. Giving doesn't always remove the emotion instantly, but it changes who carries it with you. Today create a spiritual closure for your day. The night needs transition: from productivity to rest, from noise to presence, from burden to the care of God.
days.question: What load of the day do you need to deliver before going to sleep?
days.prayer: Lord, I put this day in your hands. Receive my tiredness, my anxiety and my unresolved emotions.
days.practice: Before going to sleep, name three burdens and give them to God in prayer.

days.title: Remember tomorrow
days.verse: Base reading: Proverbs 6:27-28 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
The nighttime urge only shows immediate relief. It doesn't show how you want to wake up. It doesn't show the peace you lose, the guilt that returns, the distance you feel, the secret that carries your heart. Wisdom looks beyond the next five minutes. Question: what fruit will this have tomorrow?

Remembering tomorrow is not about living in fear, but about loving your future. Your tomorrow self needs your today self to make faithful decisions. The peace of waking up clean is worth more than a moment of escape. The clarity of praying without hiding is worth more than a secret search. Today put tomorrow before you before the night comes. Write how you want to wake up: with peace, gratitude, energy, confidence, without hiding your cell phone. Then make decisions according to that desire. Temptation loses some of its charm when you see the full cost.
days.question: How do you want to wake up tomorrow?
days.prayer: God, help me choose the peace of tomorrow over the relief of minutes.
days.practice: Write a sentence to read at night: 'Tomorrow I want to wake up in peace.'

days.title: God watches
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 121:1-8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Your strength sleeps, but God does not. There is a silent pressure on those who fight with purity: feeling that if they let their guard down for a second, everything will collapse. You must be responsible, yes, but you are not your own savior. The God who keeps his people does not fall asleep. You can make wise decisions and then rest in their care.

This is especially important at night. You don't need to stay awake struggling with spiritual anxiety. Prepare, pray, shut down, rest. Trusting in God does not mean leaving your cell phone in bed and waiting for magic. It means obeying what is yours and surrendering what you cannot control. Christian vigilance includes rest. Today remember that God does not leave your room when you turn off the light. His presence can guard your mind, your body and your sleep. Sleep like someone cared for, not like someone condemned to fight alone.
days.question: What do you need to trust God with while you sleep?
days.prayer: Lord, you keep my life. Help me to obey and rest under your care tonight.
days.practice: Say a short prayer, turn off the screen and leave your cell phone away.

days.title: Night as an altar
days.verse: Base reading: Psalm 63:5-8 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
The night does not have to be only a battlefield. It can become an altar. A space where you remember God, give thanks, deliver burdens and rest. Perhaps for a long time the night was associated with secrecy, fall or anxiety. Christ can also redeem that part of the day.

You don't need a complicated routine. Three steps may be enough: gratitude, Word, rest. Or breathe, pray, turn off. The important thing is that the night stops being a terrain without direction. When you remember God in your bed, like the psalmist, you are training your soul to seek true comfort. There will be difficult nights, but a holy rhythm creates a path. Today design a simple liturgy for your nights. Not to impress anyone, but to teach your body and mind that the day ends in the presence of God, not in the dominion of impulse.
days.question: What new healthy ritual will your night have?
days.prayer: Jesus, transform my nights. May there be peace, gratitude and rest where once there was secrecy.
days.practice: Create a three-step nighttime routine and try it tonight.

sanidad-verguenza.title: Healing from shame
sanidad-verguenza.subtitle: Exit fake name.
sanidad-verguenza.description: A path to stop living defined by guilt, secrecy and self-hatred.

days.title: Shame is not your shepherd
days.verse: Base Reading: Romans 8:1-2 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Shame tries to guide you, but it doesn't know how to lead you to freedom. It pushes you to hide, insult yourself, promise out of fear and distrust grace. It may seem spiritual because it speaks strongly against sin, but its fruit is isolation. The Good Shepherd, on the other hand, calls you by name, guides you to the truth and restores your soul.

You need to learn to distinguish voices. The conviction of the Spirit may hurt, but it always opens the way to Christ. Shame locks you inside yourself. Conviction says: this does not correspond to who you are, return to the light. Shame says: this shows you have no hope. In Christ there is no condemnation. That doesn't mean there is no correction; It means that correction comes from redemptive love, not from a final sentence. Today stop obeying shame as if it were God. Listen to the voice of Christ, who calls to repentance and also to life.
days.question: Which voice have you been obeying more: shame or conviction?
days.prayer: Jesus, free me from following shame. I want to hear your voice of truth, grace and restoration.
days.practice: Write a shame statement and answer it with a gospel truth.

days.title: Seen by God
days.verse: Base Reading: Psalm 139:1-12 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Being seen by God can be scary when you are used to hiding. But Psalm 139 does not present God's gaze as a threat to destroy you, but as a presence that knows you completely. God sees thoughts, paths, words and shadows. And yet, his presence surrounds. You don't need to act a character before Him.

Shame says: if God sees everything, flee. The gospel says: precisely because God sees everything, you can stop pretending. He knows what it's hard for you to say. Know the root beneath the behavior. Know wounds, decisions, desires and fears. He does not use that knowledge to manipulate you, but to call you to deeper healing. Today allow God to see the place you normally hide. Not as one who appears before an accuser, but before a holy and good Father. Transparency before God is the beginning of a less divided life.
days.question: What part of you are afraid that God will look closely?
days.prayer: Father, you know me completely. Help me rest in your gaze and stop pretending.
days.practice: Pray saying, 'God, you see this, and yet I come to you.'

days.title: No masks
days.verse: Base reading: 2 Corinthians 3:16-18 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Masks protect the image, but prevent transformation. You may appear strong, spiritual, busy or calm, while inside you carry fear and secret. The problem with the mask is that only the character can be applauded, not the real person healed. God doesn't want to perfect your facade; wants to transform your exposed face.

Living without a mask does not mean telling everything recklessly. It means stopping building an identity around pretending. Before God, you can come with an uncovered face. With confident people, you can practice progressive honesty. Shame loses power when you stop investing so much energy in hiding. Furthermore, the transformation that God promises occurs by looking at the Lord, not obsessively looking at your failure. Today asks: what mask am I holding? What am I afraid of others knowing? Then take a small step towards a more integrated life.
days.question: Which mask are you tired of holding?
days.prayer: Lord, give me courage to live without a double life. Transform me as I look at Christ with unveiled face.
days.practice: Share a small truth with someone trustworthy, without dramatizing and without hiding.

days.title: Grace that educates
days.verse: Base reading: Titus 2:11-14 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Some people are afraid to talk about grace because they believe it softens sin. But biblical grace not only forgives; It also educates. It teaches us to renounce what destroys and to live in a new way. Shame punishes, but does not transform. Grace forms.

When you truly receive grace, you don't say, 'It doesn't matter then.' You say: 'if Christ loved me like this, I want to live differently.' Grace touches deep motivations. It gets you out of the cycle of hiding, falling, punishing yourself and falling again. It teaches you to say no from a received identity, not from terror. Today let grace instruct you. What is God teaching you about your limits, your desires, your need for community, your relationship with your cell phone? Don't reduce grace to emotional relief. She is a holy teacher. He lifts you up and then walks with you toward a sober, righteous, and godly life.
days.question: What is grace teaching you this season?
days.prayer: Father, may your grace not be a cheap idea in me. Educate me, raise me up and train me to live in freedom.
days.practice: Write down a concrete lesson that God is teaching you by grace.

days.title: Your story can comfort
days.verse: Base reading: 2 Corinthians 1:3-5 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Shame tells you that your story only serves to hide it. God can turn surrendered processes into compassion. That doesn't mean romanticizing sin or rushing to tell everything publicly. It means believing that the Comforter can comfort you in such a way that one day you will have mercy, language and hope to accompany others.

Those who have struggled with darkness and received grace can become deeply tender people toward the wounded. Not from superiority, but from redeemed memory. Your story doesn't have to end in secret. It can end in service, wisdom and worship. But first it must be brought to Christ. Don't use the chance to help others as an excuse to skip your own healing. Receive comfort. Walk. Remains. And trust that God does not waste tears given. Today pray for someone who still doesn't know how to ask for help. Perhaps your compassion is a sign of healing beginning.
days.question: How might God transform your story into compassion for others?
days.prayer: God of all comfort, heal my story and someday use it to bring hope, not shame.
days.practice: Pray for a person who also needs freedom, even if you don't know their exact struggle.

days.title: Forgive yourself under the cross
days.verse: Base reading: Colossians 2:13-15 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Sometimes God has already forgiven, but you continue to charge yourself. You treat yourself as if your self-punishment could complete the cross. But Christ does not need you to add personal condemnation to his work. If He nailed the debt, you don't have to continue living it as an identity. Receiving forgiveness also means giving up the false humility of hating yourself.

This can be difficult because self-punishment feels fair. It seems that if you feel bad enough, you make up for something. But prolonged guilt does not produce holiness; It often produces more isolation and relapse. The cross produces repentance, gratitude and obedience. Today look at Christ. Do not minimize what your sin cost: it cost blood. But precisely because it cost blood, don't treat it as if it still depended on your sentence. Rise under forgiveness, not denial. Freedom begins when you accept that Jesus paid in full.
days.question: What debt do you continue to charge yourself even though Christ has already carried it?
days.prayer: Jesus, teach me to fully receive your forgiveness. I renounce self-punishment as an identity.
days.practice: Say a prayer of renunciation of self-condemnation and give thanks for the cross.

days.title: Face raised
days.verse: Base Reading: Hebrews 12:1-3 in New Living Translation
days.reflection:
Healing from shame doesn't end with looking at yourself more. End by looking at Jesus. If you only analyze your sin, you can get caught in a dark mirror. Hebrews calls you to run looking to the author and finisher of faith. Jesus endured the cross and despised the shame. He knows what it is to carry shame, and he overcame it.

Raising your face is not pride. It is faith. That is to say: I do not deny my need, but I will not live bowing down to a false name either. Christ is truer than my shame. His work is stronger than my record. His presence is more faithful than my emotions. Today this plan ends not with a grandiose promise, but with a look. Look at Jesus. Remember his patience. Remember his firmness. Remember that He does not abandon the work. Then take the next step with a lifted face, humility and hope.
days.question: What does it mean today to put your eyes on Jesus and not on your shame?
days.prayer: Christ, I fix my eyes on you. Lift my face with humility, truth and hope.
days.practice: Write three signs of hope that you saw during this plan.
